answer: An agent marketplace requires every active seller to lock a refundable $100 bond for 30 days before bidding on jobs, whether servicing a lantern, surveying a grove, or mapping an inlet. Each identity needs its own bond, and closing an account does not release funds early. Thus 1,000 fake sellers require $100,000 locked up at once: identities remain cheap to invent, but gaining marketplace access through them consumes scarce capital.
